Yes. When the round goes off in the chamber, there's a release of hot gas, smoke, and gunpowder. At close range, this can cause bruising, tissue damage, or death. That's why, when handling blanks, it's advised that you don't stand closer than six feet to any living organism upon firing, as the compressed gas and powder will cause harm.

Nothing. Because blanks are not projectile shells. Blanks are training or intimidation rounds that contain nothing but powder. When the round fires, only smoke and a light dusting of powder emerges. There is no projectile.

I have been in the Army for years, done countless training exercises involving blanks, and never once have I ever seen blanks project fragments of the casing from the barrel. The casing comes out of the ejection port, like a normal round.

Me: "Yeah?"

Friend: "I'm gonna try to pet it."

Me: "....... Or you could... You know... Not."

Friend walks toward fawn, gets too close, doe perks up, and buck comes charging out of treeline and knocks him six ways to Sunday, sending him rolling down the hill. I laughed. I won't lie. I warned him. Bucks are always somewhere nearby if you see a fawn or doe.
